name: mistral.rs
notable_features: Rust engine built on Hugging Face Candle, shipping as a single prebuilt binary with a Rust crate and a Python package
Serves both OpenAI-compatible /v1 and Anthropic Messages endpoints from one process, with a built-in web UI at /ui
Full multimodal in one engine: text, vision, video, audio, speech generation, image generation and embeddings
Its own UQFF quantization format plus ISQ (in-situ quantization), plus GGUF and GPTQ loading
Multi-GPU via NCCL tensor parallelism with P2P layer mapping, plus multi-node and ring attention
Built-in agentic runtime: web search, local Python and shell execution, MCP integration, OpenAI-compatible Skills bundles
mistralrs tune recommends quantization and device mapping from the model config and detected hardware; mistralrs doctor diagnoses CUDA/Metal issues
hardware_caveats: CUDA is the only accelerated Linux path; the prebuilt binary matrix is Metal on Apple Silicon, per-GPU CUDA or CPU on Linux, and CPU-only on Windows. Windows therefore has no GPU acceleration out of the box
Optional cuTile acceleration requires NVIDIA's separately installed tileiras tool, so the fastest CUDA path is not self-contained
Accelerator-specific Python wheels (CUDA, Metal, MKL, Accelerate) are separate artifacts from the main package, so an install can silently land without acceleration

Its published BF16 prefill/decode comparisons against vLLM are self-reported and mixed: it wins on Gemma 4 E4B across GB10/B200/H100 but loses badly on the 26B-A4B MoE at prefill (e.g. 2766 vs 26295 tok/s on H100 SXM), so do not generalise from the small dense model
The supported-models reference is generated from the loader registry, so coverage is exactly what that registry lists - 45+ architectures as claimed, with no fallback for the rest
best_for: A single Rust binary with OpenAI plus Anthropic API parity and a built-in web UI
Mixed text/vision/video/audio workloads in one process
Embedders that want an inference engine as a library with both Rust and Python surfaces
avoid_for: Multi-node MoE at scale, where the published numbers trail vLLM substantially
Windows GPU inference, which the prebuilt matrix covers only on CPU
Anyone needing a comparable, third-party-measured benchmark record for this engine
notes: Benchmark figures in the README are project self-reported for v0.8.2 (mean tok/s, decode 256 generated tokens, prompt lengths 128-16384) and were not independently reproduced. 'isq' is the project's own in-situ quantization; 'uqff' is its UQFF format. Block-diffusion text generation (DiffusionGemma) is integrated with paged attention and prefix caching per the README. ||| MAINTENANCE (dated fact, GitHub API, 2026-10-04): last commit 2026-10-01 (0.1 months before this record), latest release v0.9.4 published 2026-09-24, 97 contributors (distinct committers including anonymous), open_issues_count 400 (issues PLUS pull requests - see [[ev-github-open-issues-count-includes-pull-requests]]), not archived, 7733 stars.
